claims.claim: A multi-character nonempty colonless raw header line can create a fabricated entry.
claims.reason: indexOf returns -1, slice(0,-1) drops the last character, and slice(0) supplies the whole original value. For example a raw helper input abc yields key ab/value abc. A one-character line instead yields an empty key and is ignored; the finding says can, not every line. The XHR browser platform may reject/normalize malformed wire headers, so actual server-to-browser reachability is not certified.

claims.claim: The selected data-URI HTTP path allocates the complete decoded body without configured size limits.
claims.reason: fromDataURI captures and decodes the full body before Buffer allocation. The HTTP adapter invokes it in an early data: branch that returns before the normal maxContentLength/maxBodyLength controls. A large caller-selected URL can therefore consume resource outside those limits. This is not proof that an application exposes the URL to a remote attacker.

claims.claim: A crafted FormData field path can write to Object.prototype.
claims.reason: The path tokenizer preserves __proto__ and recursion starts from {}. For __proto__[polluted], target.__proto__ resolves to Object.prototype and isObject accepts it, so recursion reaches the terminal assignment on that shared prototype. The own-property check protects only terminal collisions. formToJSON and the JSON FormData transform expose selected callable entry points; no external attacker authorization path is assumed.

The claim does not establish that attackers control configuration or a remote regex-DoS.

claims.reason: For a rejected 3xx status, floor(status/100)-4 is -1, outside the two-element code array. AxiosError only sets a truthy code, so it is absent. claims.claim: A throwing cancellation listener prevents remaining notification and cleanup.
claims.reason: The promise callback invokes listeners in reverse order without try/finally or per-listener isolation, and nulls the list only after the loop. A subscribed throwing listener therefore prevents earlier listeners from running and keeps the array reachable on the token. The subscribe method imposes no isolation; a transport callback or direct subscriber can throw.

Normal CancelToken supplies a truthy CanceledError without type and bypasses this branch.
